The best in Islam is feeding people and greeting those one knows and does not know, and the best Muslim is he from whose tongue and hand Muslims are safe.
The best deeds are faith in Allah, jihad and an accepted Hajj, or prayer on time, kindness to parents and jihad; the costliest slave is best to free.
Double reward is for one of the People of the Book accepting the Prophet, a slave true to Allah and master, and a man who frees and marries his bondswoman.
Cleanliness is half of faith, praising Allah fills the scale, prayer is light, charity proof, endurance brightness, and the Quran a proof for or against you.
Frequent prostration raises a degree and removes a sin with each one, and the Prophet told Rabi'a, who asked for his company in Paradise, to help him by prostrating often.
Angels gather at the dawn and afternoon prayers; believers will see their Lord as they see the moon, and whoever keeps these two prayers will enter Paradise, not the Fire.
Allah loves best deeds done constantly, even if small; the Prophet had Zainab's prayer rope untied and, about a woman praying all night, said to do what one can sustain.
Those spending pairs for Allah are called through Paradise's gates, the Prophet hoping Abu Bakr would be called through all; one day Abu Bakr did four deeds that bring Paradise.
Allah shades seven on the Day with no other shade, among them a just ruler, a youth raised in worship, one devoted to mosques, and a secret giver of charity.
A slave who serves his master and worships Allah well has two rewards; but for jihad, Pilgrimage and his mother, Abu Huraira would have preferred to die a slave.
A day and night on watch beats a month of fasting and night prayer; whoever dies at it earns its reward forever and is spared the grave's torment.

Allah relieves whoever relieves a brother's distress, conceals the faults of one who conceals, eases Paradise's path for a seeker of knowledge, and sends tranquillity on gatherings studying the Quran.
